content.text: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: Telugu Language Evolution & Temple Architecture

The Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi (624–1075 CE) ruled coastal Andhra for over five centuries, providing the political and cultural foundation for modern Telugu identity. Founded by Kubja Vishnuvardhana, the dynasty nurtured the emergence of Telugu as a classical literary language, witnessed the pioneering Mahabharata translation by Adikavi Nannaya Bhatta, and erected magnificent Vesara-Dravidian temples at Draksharama, Biccavolu, and Chebrolu.

Milestones of Eastern Chalukyan Governance & Cultural Renaissance
rows: Vengi (Pedavegi); younger brother of Pulakesin II.
Assumed title 'Vishamasiddhi'; established autonomous sovereignty over coastal Andhra.
Initiated transition from rock-cut to structural temples.
Vengi; Greatest military monarch; defeated Rashtrakuta Krishna II and Chedis of Dahala.
Court general Panduranga set up the Addanki Inscription (848 CE) containing the earliest known Telugu verse (Taruvoja metre).
Constructed numerous Shiva shrines across coastal Andhra.
Vengi; repelled Rashtrakuta invasions after fighting 360 battles.
Patronized Telugu scholars and poets; issued Dharmavaram inscription (first Telugu Sisa metre verse).
Constructed the colossal twin Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama (Draksharama Bhimeswara) and Chalukya Bhimavaram (Samarlakota).
Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram) on Godavari river; married Chola princess Ammanga Devi.
Court was the cradle of classical Telugu literature; patronized Adikavi Nannaya Bhatta who commenced the Telugu Mahabharata translation (Andhra Mahabharatamu).
Embellished Rajahmundry as the cultural capital of Andhra; unified Chalukya-Chola lineages under son Kulottunga I.

items: Evolution of Telugu Inscriptions: Erragudipadu Inscription (575 CE) of Renati Chola king Dhananjaya is the earliest epigraph written entirely in the Telugu prose language (Kamalanadu, Kadapa district); followed by Eastern Chalukyan verse inscriptions at Addanki (Taruvoja metre), Kandukur (first Madhyakkara metre), and Bezwada (Yuddhamalla's inscription).

Nannaya Bhatta (Adikavi): Translated the first two and a half Parvas (Adi, Sabha, and part of Aranya Parva) of the Mahabharata from Sanskrit into chaste Telugu; authored 'Andhra Sabda Chintamani' (first Telugu grammatical work written in Sanskrit); hailed as 'Vaganusasana' (Lawgiver of Language).

Biccavolu Temple Complex: Located in East Godavari; cluster of 9th-century granite temples (Goluthesvara, Rajaraja, Chandrasekhara) showcasing mature Eastern Chalukyan sculpture and elegant vimana superstructures.
Chalukya-Chola Union: In 1070 CE, Rajendra Chalukya (son of Rajaraja Narendra) ascended the Chola throne in Thanjavur as Kulottunga Chola I, merging the Eastern Chalukya and Imperial Chola crowns.

content.text: Part A: Mains Analytical & Descriptive Questions

items:
Trace the evolution of the Telugu language and literature under the patronage of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi. Evaluate the seminal contribution of Nannaya Bhatta in founding classical Telugu literature. (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Trace linguistic epigraphy from pre-Chalukyan times (Bhattiprolu Brahmi, Amaravati Prakrit) to the Erragudipadu inscription (575 CE); highlight Eastern Chalukyan epigraphic verses (Addanki, Dharmavaram, Bezwada) showcasing poetic metres (Taruvoja, Sisa); analyze the historic context of Rajahmundry under Rajaraja Narendra; explain Adikavi Nannaya Bhatta's translation of the Mahabharata (Andhra Mahabharatamu): establishing Sanskrit-Telugu (Tatsama) linguistic synthesis, metric elegance (Champukavya style), and cultural legitimation; discuss his Sanskrit grammar of Telugu ('Andhra Sabda Chintamani'); conclude on how this established the foundation of Telugu classical identity.

content.text: Part B: Screening / Prelims Objective Questions

items:
Q1. Which inscription from Kadapa district, issued by Renati Chola king Dhananjaya in 575 CE, is recognized as the earliest epigraph in the Telugu language?
(a) Addanki Inscription
(b) Erragudipadu Inscription
(c) Kalamalla Inscription
(d) Bezwada Inscription
Correct Answer: (c) Kalamalla Inscription [Explanation: The Kalamalla inscription (575 CE) of Erikal Mutthuraju Dhananjaya is the earliest epigraphical record written entirely in archaic Telugu prose, closely followed by Erragudipadu.]

Q2. The Addanki Inscription (848 CE), issued during the reign of Eastern Chalukya King Gunaga Vijayaditya, is renowned in Telugu literature for containing the earliest example of:
(a) Sisa metre
(b) Taruvoja metre
(c) Kanda metre
(d) Champu style
Correct Answer: (b) Taruvoja metre [Explanation: The Addanki stone inscription of general Panduranga contains the earliest known Telugu poetic verse composed in the 'Taruvoja' classical metre.]

Q3. Adikavi Nannaya Bhatta commenced the translation of the Sanskrit Mahabharata into Telugu ('Andhra Mahabharatamu') under the royal patronage of which Eastern Chalukya king?
(a) Gunaga Vijayaditya
(b) Chalukya Bhima I
(c) Rajaraja Narendra
(d) Kubja Vishnuvardhana
Correct Answer: (c) Rajaraja Narendra [Explanation: Nannaya Bhatta, the poet laureate of Rajamahendravaram, translated the Adi, Sabha, and Aranya parvas under the patronage of King Rajaraja Narendra (1022–1061 CE).]

Q4. The magnificent Draksharama Bhimeswara Swamy Temple in East Godavari was constructed by which illustrious Eastern Chalukya monarch?
(a) Kubja Vishnuvardhana
(b) Chalukya Bhima I
(c) Jayasimha I
(d) Gunaga Vijayaditya
Correct Answer: (b) Chalukya Bhima I [Explanation: Chalukya Bhima I (892–921 CE) built the colossal two-storeyed Bhimeswara Swamy temples at Draksharama and Samarlakota to commemorate his battlefield victories.]

Q5. Which Eastern Chalukya prince married the Chola princess Ammanga Devi and unified the Eastern Chalukya and Imperial Chola thrones in 1070 CE as Kulottunga Chola I?
(a) Vimaladitya
(b) Rajaraja Narendra
(c) Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I)
(d) Danarnava
Correct Answer: (c) Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I) [Explanation: Son of Rajaraja Narendra and Chola princess Ammanga Devi, Rajendra Chalukya ascended the imperial throne at Gangaikondacholapuram as Kulottunga I in 1070 CE.]
